title: Canonical boundary composition mate and its dualizing specializations
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be morphisms of schemes. Work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and their bounded-below full subcategories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Assume compactifications of $f$, $g$ and $f;g$ [def-nagata-compactification], quasi-compactness of $f;g$, and quasi-compactness of $Y$ and $S$. Use the compactification-independent compact-support functors $F_h=Rh_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and their ordinary ambient etale right adjoints $G_h=h^\times$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $G_h^+$ for the restriction of this actual right adjoint to $D^+$ and $b_h:F_h^+\dashv G_h^+$ for the restriction of its actual ambient adjunction along the fully faithful $D^+$ inclusions. Define
$$\theta_{f,g}:G_{f;g}^+\xrightarrow{\sim}G_g^+;G_f^+$$
to be the conjugate mate of the canonical bounded-below compact-support composition $F_f^+;F_g^+\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f;g}^+$ under $b_{f;g}$ and the composite adjunction $b_f;b_g$.

Let $C_W=\nu_W^*$ be the exact derived site-comparison inverse image [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], with derived adjunction unit $\eta_W:1\to R\nu_{W,*}C_W$ for the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $P_h=C_XG_hR\nu_{Y,*}$ be the specified pro-etale exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $H\in D^+(Y_e,A)$ define $\rho_{h,H}:C_XG_hH\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hC_YH$ as $C_XG_h(\eta_{Y,H})$. Let $A_S^+$ be the degree-zero constant coefficient object in $D^+(S_e,A)$, and put $\omega_{W,e}=G_{a_W}A$ and $\omega_{W,p}=P_{a_W}A$ for a compactifiable structure map $a_W:W\to S$. Define $\lambda_W:C_W\omega_{W,e}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{W,p}$ as $\rho_{a_W,A}$ followed by the canonical comparison identification of the coefficient units.

For a bounded-below etale $H$, define the pro-etale composition $P_fP_gC_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f;g}C_SH$ by the ordered composite $P_f(\rho_{g,H}^{-1})$, then $\rho_{f,G_gH}^{-1}$, then $C_X(\theta_{f,g,H}^{-1})$, then $\rho_{f;g,H}$. Define the etale dualizing identification $\kappa_e:G_f\omega_{Y,e}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,e}$ as the value of $\theta_{f,g}^{-1}$ at $A_S^+$, included into the ambient category. Define the pro-etale dualizing identification $\kappa_p:P_f\omega_{Y,p}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,p}$ by the ordered composite $P_f(\lambda_Y^{-1})$, $\rho_{f,\omega_{Y,e}}^{-1}$, $C_X\kappa_e$, and $\lambda_X$. For $f=i$ closed and $g=a_T$ these are the specified boundary dualizing identifications.

Finally define the composition-compatibility predicate to be the conjunction of (i) the equation saying that the counit for $F_{f;g}^+\dashv G_{f;g}^+$, preceded by compact-support composition, equals the pasted counits after applying $\theta_{f,g}$, and (ii) naturality of the displayed pro-etale composition in every morphism of bounded-below etale inputs. This defines the predicate and the canonical comparison data; it does not assert that the compatibility predicate holds.

lean.statement:
noncomputable def boundaryCompositionIso {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g]
    [HasCompactification (f ≫ g)] [QuasiCompact (f ≫ g)] [CompactSpace Y] [CompactSpace S] :
    boundaryUpperShriekPlus Λ (f ≫ g) ≅
      boundaryUpperShriekPlus Λ g ⋙ boundaryUpperShriekPlus Λ f
